title: Roadmap
summary: Milestone plan sequencing architecture sign-off, the orchestration bake-off, an end-to-end iReport run, and optimization, with exit criteria and current status per item.
scope: Milestone 1 — architecture sign-off and the orchestration decision
1a architecture package (component architecture, library inventory, data contracts, authority-routing model)
1c orchestration bake-off (LangGraph, Strands Agents SDK, hand-rolled Python)
Milestone 2 — orchestrator produces an iReport end to end
deterministic validators (schema, citation, policy effectivity, prohibited content)
ASAP mock delivery outbox with idempotency key
notes: Type and precedence supplied by manifest (PRD, precedence 2) and treated as authoritative; heuristic reading agrees it is a planning/requirements document rather than a decision record — it defers all locked decisions to ADRs (notably ADR-012) and docs/DECISIONS.md. Required-reading file agents/gsd-doc-classifier.md does not exist in this repo. Output filename uses a path-derived disambiguator ('-docs') rather than a SHA-256 prefix because no shell tool was available to compute the hash; the name is still unique within OUTPUT_DIR.

milestones.name: Architecture sign-off and the orchestration decision
milestones.goal_verbatim: produce an architecture the program can sign off on, with the orchestration framework chosen on evidence rather than assertion.
milestones.status: Orchestration decision made 2026-08-11 (LangGraph, ADR-012 Accepted). Only the 1a component-architecture write-up remains open.

sub_milestones.name: Architecture package
sub_milestones.exit_criteria_verbatim: Exit: program leadership can sign off on components, libraries, and contracts.
sub_milestones.status_verbatim: Status: contracts ready for sign-off; the component-architecture write-up is outstanding.

items.item: Component architecture with the boundaries that matter marked: what is ours, what the AWS ingestion pipeline owns, what ASAP owns, and where the human review gate sits.
items.blocking: Last item blocking program sign-off on 1a

items.item: Library and framework inventory with versions, and the reason each one is there.
items.detail: Covered by the 1b scan's measured footprint and version tables; the non-orchestration layers still need writing up.

items.item: Data contracts as Pydantic models with generated JSON Schema: case, document, evidence, finding, run manifest, human disposition, ASAP envelope.
items.detail: Thirteen contracts in packages/domain/, published to schemas/, documented in docs/handoff/contracts.md; 56 tests. Deferred: ChunkRecord, EntityCandidate, TimelineEvent, PolicyRecord (blocked on Q-02) and SpecialistResult (deferred until ADR-012 resolved).

items.item: The authority-routing model: how a case maps to 5 CFR 731 suitability/fitness, SEAD-4, or both.

sub_milestones.name: Orchestration landscape scan
sub_milestones.detail: ADR-012 candidate set amended: PydanticAI/Pydantic Graph dropped; AutoGen and Semantic Kernel removed (maintenance mode since April 2026); Microsoft Agent Framework, DBOS, Temporal, Restate recorded as considered-and-not-spiked. Four candidates became three. Added three spike deliverables to 1c and raised Q-14.

sub_milestones.name: Orchestration bake-off (partial spike)
sub_milestones.exit_criteria_verbatim: Exit met (2026-08-11). ADR-012 is Accepted: the orchestration framework is LangGraph.
sub_milestones.detail: All three candidates built and passing. LangGraph selected on durable checkpointing cost (two lines with PostgresSaver vs 56 hand-rolled, 166 Strands), ~192 net wiring lines, and the only written semver commitment. Hand-rolled is recorded runner-up and fallback; Strands dominated except on AWS alignment. Both spikes retained.
carried_forward: Cold start and packaging under SAM local — unmeasured for all three, the number most likely to reopen the choice; spikes/test_scorecard.py fails the moment it is recorded.
Model-call-level idempotency (blueprint 8.5 duplicate-query detection) — owed by all three candidates, built by none.

milestones.name: The orchestrator produces an iReport
milestones.goal_verbatim: the general orchestrator runs end to end and produces an iReport from a single sub-agent query — the simplest path that touches every seam, before any optimization.
milestones.exit_criteria_verbatim: Exit: one command takes a synthetic case to a delivered, human-approved iReport. Every seam has been exercised once.
items: Orchestrator on LangGraph (ADR-012), behind our own port so nodes never import it directly
Model-call-level idempotency (blueprint 8.5 duplicate-query detection) — owed by every 1c candidate and built by none; a crash mid-fan-out currently re-runs an in-flight model call
One synthetic case, ingested locally and indexed into local OpenSearch
Authority routing selects the policy pack
A single specialist sub-agent query produces proposed findings against one criterion
Deterministic validators: schema, citation resolution, policy effectivity, prohibited content
Human review gate — run pauses, disposition recorded, run resumes
Delivery to the ASAP mock through the outbox with an idempotency key

milestones.name: Optimize
milestones.goal_verbatim: Widen and deepen against measurements from M2, in the order the evidence justifies.
milestones.detail: No exit criteria stated. Candidates: the full specialist set across both authority families; retrieval quality work (hybrid fusion, query planning, reranking); the contradiction and challenge stages; multi-criterion fan-out; model-tier tuning across the three aliases; the evaluation harness and red-team scenarios. Sequence from M2 findings — not from this list.

milestones.name: The handoff package
milestones.goal_verbatim: Built as we go, not written up at the end (ADR-001)

docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md — what remains unresolved and what it would cost to be wrong
